**Firmify** ([www.firmify.in](http://www.firmify.in)) **– Tech Developer Inputs** 

**1\. Overall Requirement**

We are trying to create an Indian version of [**wonder.legal**](https://www.wonder.legal/) and offer contracts and policies for download by the user. 

The domain is booked, trademarks applied for, website pages and documents to be covered, header and footer have been decided at my end and now the developer is required to build the Firmify website where users can select legal documents, answer guided questions, preview the document, make payment or use a subscription pack and download the final completed document. Sample: [https://www.wonder.legal/in/creation-modele/employment-agreement-in](https://www.wonder.legal/in/creation-modele/employment-agreement-in) 

Firmify will be positioned as an online platform for downloading law firm drafted and certified contracts and policies. As per my level of understanding \- it will be a document automation website with dynamic templates, conditional logic, clause-level options, payment/download gating, user dashboard, subscription access, SEO-friendly public pages and protected paid document content. 

*USP: Law-firm-vetted and legally enforceable documents that establish trust, offered through a simple-to-use platform where they can be easily filled with guidance and downloaded \+ e-signed to remove user fatigue \- and affordably priced for users who do not want to incur law-firm/lawyer fees.*

**2\. User Journey:** The User journey of Firmify is provided below for developer’s implementation:

1. User lands on the homepage, All Documents page, category page, dedicated main page or individual document page – every document will have a landing page. 

2. User searches for or selects a document.

3. User starts the document creation flow.

4. User answers guided questions.

5. Platform displays guidance notes and clause options wherever applicable.

6. Platform applies dynamic fields and conditional logic based on the user’s answers.

7. User can save the document as a draft.

The text for all drafts will be provided by us. All text and layout for all pages including header/footer etc. will be prepared based on the keywords and discussions with Navins team. 

8. User can see a progress bar during the document creation process (either showing percentage as shown in the image or number of questions answered, ex: 4 out of 6 questions.

9. User reaches the preview stage.

10. Create restricted preview functionality before payment or subscription unlock. Preview may be blurred, locked, watermarked or partially restricted. The final document must not be downloadable before payment, subscription access or approved entitlement. After successful unlock, allow download in Word and PDF formats.

11. User makes payment or uses an active subscription pack.

12. User downloads the final document in Word and/or PDF format.

13. E-signing will be integrated in the platform so users will have the option to either fill, save and print or fill, e-sign and send to the other party signing the document. 

14. Completed document is saved in the user dashboard.

15. Unfinished documents remain visible in the dashboard.

16. Returning users are prompted to continue unfinished documents.

The text for all website pages, layout, header, footer, document mapping and subscription pack details are attached with these inputs and are to be used while building the website.

**10\. Conditional Logic and Clause-Level Guidance**

The platform must support document-specific conditional logic. This means that each document will have its own questionnaire, and the user’s answers will decide what information is inserted, which clauses are included, and which parts of the final document are removed or changed. See this link for sample: [https://www.wonder.legal/in/modele/employment-agreement-in](https://www.wonder.legal/in/modele/employment-agreement-in) 

For example:

1. If a document asks whether a probation period applies and the user selects **Yes**, the probation clause is included and the relevant probation details are inserted.

2. If the user selects **No**, the probation clause is removed from the final document.

3. If a document asks for salary, fee, rent, notice period, payment date, contract term or other details, the answers are inserted into the correct fillable fields in the document. Filling of the fields will be done in a live manner to show progress to the user. 

4. If a document gives different clause options, the selected option is inserted into the final document.

5. If a user leaves a required field blank, the platform flags the missing information before moving to the next question/screen or at the time of preview or download.

Wherever the user has to choose between clause options or answer a legally important question, display a short explanation, tooltip or guidance note so that the user understands what the answer will do in the document. These notes will be provided by us once the format etc. are agreed between the developer and us.

**12\. Website-Specific Technical Requirements**

- **Chatbot requirement:** Keep it as a small support icon with an actual human photo. The popup must not block search, navigation, page content or document creation. It must work properly on mobile.  
    
- **Text protection and SEO crawlability requirement:** Protect paid document templates, generated documents and locked previews so that users or AI cannot access, copy or download the full paid document before payment, subscription access or approved entitlement. At the same time, keep all public website pages, including the homepage, category pages, individual document pages, Resources pages, FAQs and other SEO pages, crawlable and indexable by Google. Public SEO text must remain readable by search engines and must not be converted into image-only text or blocked through JavaScript in a manner that prevents indexing. Use preview gating only for paid document content, while keeping public explanatory page content available for SEO. Implement proper heading tags, alt attributes, breadcrumbs, page and FAQ schema, sitemap, robots.txt and SEO-friendly URLs.  
    
- **Electronic signature requirement:** Integrate electronic signature functionality so the user can either download the completed document in Word/PDF format or proceed to electronically sign the generated document. The e-signature flow must connect with the completed document and allow the user to sign the document and, where applicable, send it to the other party for signature.  
    
- **Payment and unlock requirement:** Enable payment for individual document downloads and subscription pack purchases. The payment system must support:  
  a. payment gateway integration;  
  b. individual document purchase;  
  c. subscription pack purchase;  
  d. payment confirmation;  
  e. invoice / receipt generation;  
  f. coupon codes;  
  g. referral / influencer codes;  
  h. failed payment handling;  
  i. document unlock after successful payment; and  
  j. subscription upgrade prompt at checkout.  
    
- **User dashboard requirement:** Create a simple user dashboard which shows:  
  a. completed documents;  
  b. unfinished / pending documents;  
  c. drafts;  
  d. document history;  
  e. subscription status;  
  f. active pack details;  
  g. payment history;  
  h. download history;  
  i. option to resume unfinished documents; and  
  j. option to download completed documents again, subject to final business rules.  
    
  Keep open / unfinished projects visible to the user and, on return visits, prompt the user to complete unfinished documents.

**13\. Mobile Website Requirements**

**A. Overall Mobile Layout Principle:** Build the mobile website so that all desktop functionality remains available in a clean, single-column, touch-friendly layout. The mobile experience must feel simple and app-like, not like a compressed desktop website.

**Suggestions for mobile layout:** The below mentioned points are only suggestions and developer can decide what’s the best way to implement this. 

**\- Homepage Mobile Layout:** For the homepage, stack sections vertically. Use a hamburger menu for navigation. Resize the hero image to fit the mobile screen, keep the tagline centered, and convert the video/demo section into a clickable thumbnail where required. Keep the search bar full-width. Display category cards either one per row or as a horizontal scrollable row. Display quick-document cards one per row. Subscription pack teaser cards may be horizontally scrollable. Keep CTA buttons full-width.

**\- Mobile Navigation:** For navigation, use a hamburger menu with search at the top, followed by navigation links and account/dashboard links. Quick access icons may be placed inside the menu to avoid crowding the mobile header.

**\- Document Cards on Mobile:** For document cards, use one card per row with the document title, short description and action button. Tablet layouts may use two columns only where there is sufficient space.

**\- Search and Filters on Mobile:** For search and filters, collapse filters into a dropdown, accordion or collapsible panel on the All Documents page and category pages. The search bar must remain easy to access on mobile.

**\- Document Questionnaire on Mobile:** For the document questionnaire, use a single-column flow with large touch-friendly input fields. Show the progress indicator clearly, such as “Step 2 of 10” or an equivalent progress bar. Keep Previous / Next actions easy to access. A sticky bottom bar for Next / Previous buttons may be used to reduce unnecessary scrolling.

**\- Preview and Payment on Mobile:** For preview and payment, use a mobile-sized document preview/PDF viewer or a clean download flow suitable for mobile devices. Payment forms must use full-width fields and mobile-friendly payment gateway screens.

**\- Sticky Elements on Mobile:** For sticky elements, keep only essential actions sticky, such as the Next button in the questionnaire or the primary CTA where required. Avoid sticky elements that block content, forms, search or payment fields.

**\- Mobile Performance:** For performance, use lazy-loading images, compressed assets and minimal heavy JavaScript on mobile. The mobile website must load quickly and keep all important pages crawlable and indexable.

**\- Mobile Functionality:** The mobile layout must retain search, document selection, questionnaire, save draft, progress bar, preview, payment, subscription unlock, download and dashboard functionality in a simplified mobile format.
